title: Fiberlock: per-tenant GPU isolation, quota enforcement, and autoscale contracts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: implement a low-latency, enforceable tenant isolation layer (internal codename "Fiberlock") for Dedicated GPU pools that provides: 1) per-tenant throughput guarantees (contracted tokens/sec & ops/min), 2) predictable autoscaling policies that respect contracts and headroom, and 3) noisy-neighbor detection + mitigation with soft/hard quota enforcement.

Scope and user stories:
- As a P&L owner using Dedicated, I can purchase a throughput contract and see committed vs observed utilization with guarantees and overage handling.
- As an infra engineer, I can configure autoscale policies that honor tenant contracts and allocate burst capacity without affecting guaranteed lanes.
- As an SRE, I get deterministic mitigation actions for noisy tenants: shaping, temporary lane demotion, or preemptible eviction with audit logs.

Core design components: 
- Contract model: per-tenant "contract tokens" expressed as steady-state throughput (tps/tokens-per-second) + burst allowance (burst tokens and refill window). Contracts map to scheduler QoS classes.
- Fiberlock partitions: soft-silos (elastic shareable backing pool) + hard-silos (reserved GPU lanes for guaranteed contracts). Runtime enforces isolation with scheduler tokens, CUDA cgroup limits, and KV-cache affinity hints to bound interference.
- Autoscale policy types: 
  * Guaranteed-Aware Autoscale: scales pool capacity only when aggregate headroom for guaranteed lanes falls below threshold; uses lookahead forecasting (30s window) to avoid oscillation.
  * Opportunistic Autoscale: scales for best-effort/soft-silo workloads under excess capacity constraints.
- Noisy-neighbor detection: realtime classifier using per-tenant latency, GPU SM utilization spikes, memory pressure, and prefix-KV-miss rates. Policies map classifier outputs to actions (shape, lane-demote, eviction).
- Quota enforcement: soft throttles with token-bucket shaping, followed by hard enforcement via preemption policies and temporary lease removal. All actions recorded in audit logs for customer transparency.
- Observability/console: per-tenant dashboards (committed vs used), anomaly alerts, throttle traces, and a roll-forward playbook in Console for support teams.

Trade-offs we debated: 
- Strict hard-silos reduce noisy neighbor incidents but lower utilization; we opted for hybrid soft+hard approach to balance utilization and guarantees.
- Quick preemption improves SLOs for other tenants but can cause tail latency for preempted customers; we limit preemption to preemptible lanes and add throttled notifications.

Acceptance criteria (initial):
- Scheduler can allocate hard-silo lanes to tenants with a throughput contract and prevent steal under typical workloads.
- Autoscaler respects guaranteed headroom thresholds and does not scale purely for opportunistic tenants when guaranteed headroom is under threshold.
- Noisy-test harness reproduces interference; mitigation reduces P99 latency of affected tenants by >=40% within 90s of detection.
- Audit logs emitted for every mitigation action and visible in Console with tenant-friendly messages.
comments: 2026-02-25 - Design RFC posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/rfc/fiberlock-gpu-isolation (initial architecture diagrams, token model, and autoscale knobs). Feedback requested from Scheduling and Runtime teams.

2026-03-02 - PoC (single-node) completed by @Ibrahim: token-bucket shaping + CUDA cgroup enforcement. Observed reduced GPU SM contention in synthetic BERT mix (p99 latency improved 48%). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7321

2026-03-05 - Cross-team review notes: Security asked for explicit KMS audit annotations for preemption decisions; Console requested a minimal API to surface per-tenant contract state. Recorded as dependencies.

2026-03-08 - Load test results: 50-tenant mixed workload on 8xA100 cluster. With hybrid silos, cluster utilization 72% vs 81% baseline (no isolation) but SLA violations dropped from 6.2% to 0.3% for guaranteed tenants. Test artifacts: https://perf.redwood.ai/reports/fiberlock-20260308

2026-03-10 - Implementation sprint: scheduler-side token accounting merged to staging. Runtime enforcement hooks added (cuda-cgroup and lane labels). Integration test failing intermittently when autoscaler and preemption compete for capacity — created dependency ENG-827660.

2026-03-12 - Plan for next week: stabilize autoscaler race by introducing a small coordination leader step (autoscale intent window 5s). Add e2e test that simulates concurrent scale + preempt scenarios.
2026-03-13 - Blocker: final audit schema needs Security sign-off (KMS metadata) before rolling mitigation actions to prod. Ticket assigned to @Priya Rao for review.
